recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Salad with Peanut-Ginger Dressing
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon finely chopped fresh ginger root
salt and ground black pepper to taste
3.5 cups cooked chicken, cut into strips
1 red bell pepper, seeded and cut into strips
0.5 cup chopped roasted peanuts, for garnish

steps.text: To make the dressing, place the peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, chili-garlic sauce, brown sugar, ginger, red pepper flakes, and 3 tablespoons of chicken broth together in a blender or bowl of a food processor. Blend until smooth. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Thin the dressing to your taste by adding more chicken broth or water.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add the linguine and cook until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and place pasta into a large mixing bowl.

Add the chicken, carrots, green onions, red pepper, celery, and cilantro to the bowl with the linguine. Pour the dressing over the noodle-chicken mixture and toss until mixture is evenly coated. Divide the salad among eight serving plates, and sprinkle peanuts over each serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Noodle Salad with Peanut-Ginger Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Asian flavors star in this chicken-linguine pasta salad that tosses julienned carrots, celery, green onions, and cilantro with a zesty ginger-peanut-garlic seasoned dressing.

review.reviewBody: The flavor of the dressing in this recipe is just delicious! I did have to make small adjustments based on what I had on hand - no garlic-chili sauce so I just used 2 cloves of garlic and a tiny bit more red pepper flakes, warm water in place of the chicken broth and no salt, as the soy sauce added enough saltiness for my tastes. I added about 1/2 tsp. toasted sesame oil and omitted the chicken (will add some leftover from tomorrow night's dinner) and added broccoli and snow peas. A squeeze of lime and this is a perfectly seasoned dish - my only problem is the amount of dressing. I only used half the pasta (whole wheat) since I wanted more veggies, and I feel it could use just a little more of this yummy sauce. Next time I will increase that part of the recipe by half and this dish will be perfection in my book.

I made this recipe last night almost as written. I used specific name brand ingredients as listed, however, I changed the linguine to Ronzoni "Garden Delight" Enriched Carrot, Tomato & Spinach Spaghetti and it was remarkable. I changed the red bell pepper to a half jar of drained Mezzetta Deli-Sliced Roasted Red Bell Pepper strips. Yum! And most importantly, I made this salad 3 hours before dinner and refrigerated it. When the pasta finished cooking, I drained it and tossed with 2 ounces of Cilantro-Onion olive oil to prevent sticking, placed in a sealable bowl and chilled it. The vegetable ingredients were chopped added to a large bowl and chilled. I grilled the chicken breasts inside on a panini grill and chilled. When ready to serve I combined all ingredients and it came out marvelous, worthy of 10 stars if I could go that high. Thank you for sharing this recipe Sherbg. It is definately a keeper!! Andy

READ THIS: Definitely make extra sauce and cook chicken in it. Then add veggies and cook for a moment before noodles (I used rice noodles) & more sauce. Cook the sauce down some (I did in avocado oil) & add green onions and cilantro at the end. Serve with a squeeze of lime to put it over the edge. Great recipe!

Tasty and easy to prepare, this dish reminded us of our favorite Thai restaurant's peanut dressing. I added fresh minced garlic and Thai sweet red chili sauce to the recipe since I did not have garlic-chili sauce. You don't need a food processor for this recipe if you simply warm the soy sauce and chicken broth in the microwave first, which helps to melt the peanut butter. Just whisk them together until smooth. You can therefore make the sauce right in the serving bowl, making clean-up so much faster! I also added some stir-fried broccoli to this dish and next time I might also try water chesnuts for added crunch. Delicious. A definite make-again--next week!

This was VERY easy and tasty, however I did change some of the recipe. 
First of all, I doubled the ingredients in the dressing; I hate dry pasta. After I made the dressing as the recipe had written (except doubled), I tasted it and it was WAY too salty. So I added another tbsp. of brown sugar, another dose of red pepper flakes, another tsp. of chili garlic sauce, and 1 1/2 tbsp. of honey. This did the trick...the dressing was excellent!!
I added red peppers, green peppers, green onions, and julienned carrots, omitted the celery and cilantro, and it was awesome!! My husband took a bite before I put it in the fridge to chill, and I had fight him off because he loved it so much and didn't want to wait.
With the modifications, this may be the best Asian noodle salad I've ever had.

This recipe ROCKS!!!.....The flavors are wonderfully close to a resturants version we recently enjoyed. We made this as a hot dish served individually. Starting with the sauce, we doubled and heated all the ingredients in a sauce pan. Cooked the chicken and cut into strips seperate into 4 servings. Cooked the pasta al dente saving some of the pasta water, and setting it aside. In a skillet, add a small amount of the pasta water, handfuls of peanuts, shredded carrots, beans sprouts, and green onions. cook for 1 minute. Add the chicken, cook for another minute. Add desired amount of pasta for a single serving and peanut sauce. Toss in the skillet long enough to coat all with sauce. Top with cilantro and enjoy!!!

I added 1/2 cup of broth instead of 3T. I also sautéed the vegetables I had: broccoli, yellow pepper, water chestnuts and edamame. 
Family said this was delicious!

Wow - this is really good. My husband really likes spicy so I upped the chili garlic paste. I doubled the sauce the second time I made this just because he loved it so much and I had added additional veggies. Water chestnuts, more celery, red bell pepper and cucumbers. This salad is perfect for pot lucks or picnics - it is awesome at room temp. Add more broth to the sauce to acheive your desired thickness. If you have a stick blender - use it for the sauce, it blends it in a snap.

I took this to party today and it went over very well. I did cut back on the red pepper flakes since there was kids at the party and not everyone likees heat. I did find it a bit too "salty/soy saucy" so I did add probably double the broth and it was great. I also doubled the sauce as suggested and then tossed it with about 3/4 of the sauce and put the rest in a small bowel next to it for those that wanted more. I did sprinkle with chopped peanuts, but also put a small bowel with extra for those that wanted to sprinkle more on. Great recipe and I can easily see using the dressing on chicken or other things as others have suggested. Thanks for the recipe. It's a keeper.

We loved this! I substituted apple cider vinegar for the rice vinegar, but that's the only change I made. We also ate it hot (I stir fried the veggies and warmed the dressing in the micro). It was delicious!!! Will make again and again!
OK, I made it again for a luncheon, and served it cold. I made it the day before and it did get a little dry in the frig so I spruced it up with a little italian salad dressing. This worked perfectly, everyone loved it!

I thought this was very good. I used vacuum sealed fresh udon noodles instead of pasta. I felt like it was missing something so I doubled the Asian garlic-chili sauce.(I found a similar recipe that asked for 2 TBSPs of the sauce and decided to try it.) But I still thought it needed something else so I ended up adding a few drops of sesame oil to the noodles. Then I thought it was perfect. So did my husband.

This was really fabulous, even on a coldish night. We had leftover rotisserie chicken so hubby sliced it up along with the veggies. I had tinker with the dressing as it was just too thick as is. This is a personal preference things. Instead of roasted peanuts, I roasted some pine nuts tossed in sesame oil and seasoned with white pepper. So good!!!

The dressing is on the spicy side, but I enjoyed. In the past I have made a peanut dressing that had tahini in it. I think I prefer this one better and I don’t think it is as high in calories as this. I did not use linguine in this instead I substituted spiralized zucchini it was very tasty. The other substitution I made was half the amount of soy sauce was substituted with coconut amino‘s. I knew I did not have enough soy sauce when I was at the store I wanted to buy more at Trader Joe’s and they were out. I knew that the amino’s was a substitute so I used it.

This is the yummiest salad! I am so glad I tried it. It is a big hit with the entire family. I didn’t have fresh ginger, so I used pickled ginger and I also added sugar snap peas which is a must. I will add them from now on. Sooooo good!
I love main dish salads for summer dinners and this one is tops.

Made as written except that I didn't have the garlic chili sauce or the fresh ginger. I used minced garlic and extra red pepper flakes and ground ginger. It was very good. I wouldn't call it a salad though, it's more like a side/main dish. Maybe if the vegetables are cut larger, it would be more like a true salad. At any rate, it was very good when eaten slightly warm.
I make the sauce ahead and take this on camping trips and throw it all together in a wok for fast and crowd pleasing dish.
This was okay. For all of the work involved in making it there wasn't a lot of flavor.

My family went back for seconds so this is a keeper! Next time I will make a little more of the dressing (we like dishes that are a little more saucy) and probably add a little more chicken. But overall a tasty dish!
Absolutely loved it! I used a splash of sriracha, we like spicy peanut sauce and will make this again in the very near future.
